Figure 4k source counts report seizures in 5/6 Adora1 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/12 controls after D1 agonist. This receptor deletion differs from microglial CD39 deletion.

Cyclazosin treatment reduced the L-MO radial astrocyte calcium response evoked by NE-MO stimulation. Pharmacology supports alpha1B receptor involvement without proving exclusive astrocyte-specific action.

Arf6 knockdown mice had lower untreated whisker-evoked perfusion responses than littermate controls in the reported comparison. Subsequent barium reduced both responses, with a smaller reported barium-sensitive fraction in knockdown mice; no exact fraction is calibrated.

Capillary endothelial cells from inducible Arf6 knockdown mice had lower barium-sensitive Kir current density than littermate controls. Partial endothelial knockdown is distinct from complete or capillary-restricted deletion.

GTPgammaS reduced residual ATP and NAV-2729 increased it relative to their separate vehicle controls in the supplemented microvessel lysate assay. The inverse readout supports altered kinase activity, not direct endothelial membrane PIP2 measurement.

NAV-2729 reduced upstream arteriole dilation to focal capillary potassium in the ex vivo preparation relative to vehicle. Diameter is the observed endpoint; conducted voltage is inferred rather than directly recorded in this assay.

Cortical NAV-2729 reduced whisker-evoked relative perfusion. Concurrent intravenous diC16-PIP2 preserved a larger response relative to NAV alone, but did not restore the higher vehicle-treated response. Groups and pre/post comparisons remain distinct.

Pipette NAV-2729 caused a time-dependent reduction of capillary endothelial Kir currents relative to vehicle. Bath diC16-PIP2 present before recording preserved much of the current during NAV exposure; it was not a sequential rescue after current loss in the same cell.

Intravenous diC16-PIP2 increased the whisker-evoked perfusion response in Arf6 knockdown mice in a separate cohort. The nonsignificant treated-genotype contrast does not establish complete equivalence or restoration of every vascular function.

Bath diC16-PIP2 increased the measured Kir current in capillary endothelial cells from Arf6 knockdown mice relative to untreated knockdown cells. The result supports a supplementation effect without direct measurement of endogenous lipid concentration.
Partial two-photon ablation of hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced time in futility-induced passivity in selected larval zebrafish; it did not abolish all passive behavior.
Light activation of gfap-driven Opto-alpha1-AR in hindbrain radial astrocytes reduced fictive swim power relative to controls.
Capsaicin treatment of fish expressing rat TRPV1 sparsely in radial astrocytes increased passive time in closed loop; transgene-negative and saline controls did not show the same effect.

In the DG slice imaging assay, astrocyte VGLUT1 deletion reduced CNO-evoked glutamate-sensor responses. Responses were detected in a subset of tested astrocytes; exact population proportions remain unresolved.

Theta-burst LTP was lower in DG synaptic fields near recombined VGLUT1-deficient astrocytes than in neighboring unrecombined fields. Figure 3 source data contains 16 paired normalized measurements; this does not establish universal astrocyte necessity for LTP.
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVER activation produced increased downstream AVAR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, AVJR activation produced increased downstream AVDR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

The day-56 dentate assay found more retained BrdU-labeled cells after the Bax manipulation: reported means 3004 versus 11113, three mice per group. BrdU was given on days 9-18; only a subset expressed NeuN, so the total is not a count of mature functional neurons.

In the nine-day similar-context task, male NCff mice given tamoxifen had higher discrimination ratios than vehicle controls (11 versus nine mice; reported treatment P=0.023). This supports a task-specific behavioral effect; it does not directly measure neural pattern separation or general memory improvement.

Eight weeks after tamoxifen, NCff mice had more dentate DCX-positive cells and more DCX-positive cells with tertiary dendrites than vehicle controls (three mice per group). This is a marker-population response to the Bax manipulation, not a direct neuron birth-rate measurement.

In the running-housed comparison, tamoxifen-treated NCff mice showed greater open-field path length, rearing and center exploration than vehicle controls (11 versus ten mice). Changed locomotion prevents an isolated anxiety interpretation and does not establish a human therapeutic effect.

At eight weeks, the Bax manipulation increased the weak-tetanus dentate field-LTP response without bicuculline (reported treatment P=0.039). This population assay does not identify the contribution of each birthdated neuron or prove a complete cell-number mediation route.

In the 23-person fMRI behavioral sample, all tested template/violation-position conditions have above-chance detection. Across the ten template means, sensitivity decreases with assigned description cost (reported R squared 0.95), while correct-response time increases (R squared 0.85).
Selective BLA-to-CeA terminal inhibition reduces open-arm and center exploration in a separate low-stress cohort.
Selective BLA terminal activation in CeA increases open-arm and center exploration in the reported high-stress mouse preparation.
Direct BLA somatic activation decreases open-arm exploration in the reported comparison; it is not interchangeable with projection activation.
P5 microglia in C3 knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. The developmental knockout does not isolate microglial C3 production or an exclusive complement pathway.

Calca-cre nodose hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6 and IL-1beta after LPS. IL-10 did not differ significantly and is represented separately; this population does not inherit the TRPA1-associated three-analyte profile.
Focal capillary 10 mM potassium dilated the attached upstream arteriole ex vivo. Barium treatment and endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion suppressed this response in the specified comparisons.
Capillary 10 mM potassium increased upstream feed-arteriole diameter in the in vivo paired comparison. This does not imply that the stimulated capillary itself dilated.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased peak RBC flux in wild-type mice. The response was attenuated in endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 knockout and barium-treated wild-type groups; flux counts RBC passages per second.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium increased RBC velocity in the wild-type comparison; no significant increase was detected in the knockout or barium-treated comparisons. Velocity was measured in the peak-flux bin and is distinct from flux.

Focal capillary 10 mM potassium hyperpolarized upstream arteriolar smooth muscle in the isolated CaPA recording. This is a direct voltage measurement at the sampled upstream cell, not along every intervening endothelial contact.

Focal capillary potassium still increased RBC flux under cortical tetrodotoxin, while whisker-evoked flux was suppressed in the separate control comparison. Ejected potassium bypasses the physiological release step.

Separating the capillary tree from its feed arteriole removed the upstream dilatory response to capillary 10 mM potassium, while direct arteriolar potassium still evoked dilation. Continuity is supported; a particular connexin is not identified.

CPA co-treatment reduced the reported D1-challenge seizure incidence in the CD39-deletion preparation: 1/9 co-treated mice versus 9/11 in the D1-only cohort. The co-treated control cohort had 0/5 seizures.
After D1 agonist challenge, Figure 4i source counts report seizures in 9/11 CD39-deletion mice and 1/11 controls. This is a challenge-specific incidence comparison.

The CD39-deletion cohort had lower striatal adenosine-assay fluorescence after D1 agonist than controls. Figure 4h source data are relative fluorescence units, not extracellular adenosine concentrations.

AAV c-Fos shRNA attenuated ECS-associated chromatin opening at regions annotated with c-Fos binding sites compared with control shRNA. This supports a contribution to the induction response under this perturbation.

c-Fos shRNA attenuated induction of RNA for genes associated with the selected activity-responsive regions compared with control shRNA. Parallel accessibility and RNA effects do not uniquely establish that accessibility mediates the RNA response.

AAV c-Fos overexpression without ECS partially mimicked activity-associated opening at c-Fos-associated regions compared with EYFP control. It does not establish sufficiency for all activity-dependent chromatin changes.

Without ECS, c-Fos overexpression increased RNA abundance for genes associated with c-Fos-induced chromatin opening. Similar distributions of selected expression changes do not establish molecular or functional equivalence to ECS.
Perforant-path conditioning can produce persistent changes in dentate population responses.
P5 microglia in CR3/CD11b knockout mice engulfed less labeled RGC input than WT littermate controls. Engulfment persisted, so CR3 is not established as the sole route of input removal.

Ipsilateral and contralateral RGC projection territories overlapped more in CR3 knockout dLGN at P10 and P30. This is an anatomical refinement endpoint, not a direct measurement of synaptic transmission.

Juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta and total VGlut2-positive puncta were more densely represented in CR3 knockout dLGN. These structural markers do not directly measure electrical efficacy or prove a unique engulfment mechanism.
Picrotoxin exposure changes the culture event-size distribution toward a bimodal form, with recovery after washout.

Arterial endothelial Gja4/Gja5 deletion increased apparent input resistance and decreased apparent capacitance in the aortic whole-cell assay. These coupled-network measurements do not establish brain endothelial conduction velocity.

Neurobiotin loaded through a patch pipette reached fewer neighboring aortic endothelial cells after arterial Gja4/Gja5 deletion. Residual multicell fills occurred; the result is not complete elimination in every measurement.

Pial arterial diameter responses to focal visual stimulation were smaller and more spatially restricted in arterial connexin mutants. This two-photon endpoint retains a separate local diving-arteriole null.

The widefield HbT-related arterial response to focal visual stimulation showed reduced spatial extent in connexin mutants. The optical response and its fitted decay are not calibrated blood flow or a graph edge length.

Full-field visual stimulation evoked a more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related response in connexin mutants. The assay does not directly measure ATP demand, oxygen use or adequacy of metabolic supply.

Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the three full-field distance bins extending through 400-800 micrometers. The 800-1200-micrometer bin did not show a significant genotype difference.

ChRmine stimulation produced smaller, more spatially restricted arterial HbT-related responses in connexin mutants. Distance is measured from opsin expression, and the zero-laser trials can retain vascular responses.

Connexin mutants had longer optical-response time-to-peak in the five reported distance bins extending through 1200-1600 micrometers from ChRmine expression. The 1600-2000-micrometer bin is a separate nonsignificant result.

The response-onset-versus-distance calculation yielded slower arterial propagation in connexin mutants. This velocity is derived from optical vasomotion trajectories; it is neither RBC velocity nor directly measured electrical conduction.

Retinal large-artery serotonin fills were restricted to single probe cells in the sampled connexin mutants. Spreading events in controls depended on favorable loading and were observed in only two of four mice.
Dbh-cre cNST hM3Dq activation reduced circulating IL-6, IL-1beta and TNF and increased IL-10 after LPS. The four-analyte endpoint does not demonstrate that norepinephrine is the required mediator.

In the separate high-dose LPS assay, Dbh-cre cNST activation improved survival relative to mCherry controls through the plotted nine-day window. This does not establish treatment efficacy against bacterial infection or an interchangeable nodose protocol.

One hour after ECS, bulk dentate ATAC-seq identified gained-open and gained-closed regions relative to sham. Supplementary Table 4 lists 11,438 gained-open and 1,739 gained-closed regions under the publication analysis; these are genomic region counts, not neuron counts.

Across independent post-ECS cohorts, the published region lists retain 4,175 early gained-open and 484 gained-closed regions at four hours, and 597/22 respectively across one, four and 24 hours. The shared genomic regions define a sampled window; most early changes are not retained through every sampled timepoint.

Independent dentate RNA-seq samples showed increased and decreased transcript abundance one hour after ECS relative to sham. This is an RNA-abundance response, not a direct measurement of transcription rate, protein production or learning.

Five days after conditioning, exposure to the changed environment B yielded fewer Arc+/eYFP+ labeled cells per DG slice than re-exposure to training environment A. This is an effect of the environmental comparison on a marker readout, not a selective intervention establishing that the labeled cells cause memory.

The changed-context A-B group showed less freezing than the A-A group in the five-day re-exposure assay. Freezing is a behavioral readout under a multi-cue protocol; its covariance with neuronal labels does not establish a molecular mediator.
Activation of nonselective cells during the normal-contrast Go stimulus disrupts the measured Go ensemble and reduces task performance.
Activation of selected pattern-completion cells during low-contrast Go stimulation increases ensemble reliability and hit-minus-false-choice task performance.

After closed loop was replaced by probabilistic swim-triggered visual feedback, mean radial astrocyte calcium rose faster with less reliable feedback. This readout supports temporal integration without identifying a unique algorithm.
Removing the practiced force field produces reaching deviations approximately opposite to initial exposure errors.
Assistive and resistive forces change hand-localization bias differently; the study reports no significant corresponding variance difference.

Microglia contained more labeled input from the vehicle eye than from the forskolin-treated eye. The measured comparison concerns relative input engulfment within the sampled dLGN, not all neural activity or all glial cells.

After cross-fostering within 12 hours of birth, adult hippocampal bisulfite readouts at the 5-prime NGFI-A-site CpG (site 16) followed foster-mother care class. The comparison supports a postnatal environmental contribution rather than an effect fixed solely by biological-mother class.
Optogenetic activation of fast-spiking cells selectively amplifies local gamma in the reported barrel-cortex preparation.
Systemic Hcrt-R1 antagonist pretreatment reduced the 20-Hz stimulation-related shortening of post-stimulation wake latency in the reported comparison.
Hcrt-neuron photostimulation with specified trains shortens post-stimulation wake latency from SWS and REM relative to control mice; the distribution shifts rather than fixing the transition time.

Figure 4m source counts show no seizures in 10 co-treated Il34-deletion mice or 11 co-treated controls, versus 8/9 and 2/11 in their respective D1-only cohorts. The caption and workbook give inconsistent co-treatment sample counts; the stated counts are the workbook values.
The Figure 4m D1-only cohort had seizures in 8/9 Il34 flox/Drd1a-Cre mice versus 2/11 controls. Neuronal ligand deletion with reduced microglia is not a direct, acute microglial ablation.

Intraperitoneal TNF or IL-1beta and IL-10 evoked calcium responses in different observed nodose neurons during the short recording trials. The response classifier and sampled cells define the claim; direct neuronal cytokine-receptor binding is not established.

The separately irradiated Bax-floxed cohort had fewer dentate DCX-positive cells than sham controls: reported means 144 versus 3120, three mice per group. This regional intervention does not selectively isolate newborn-neuron function or by itself prove cognitive necessity.

Constitutive Tek-Cre Kcnj2 deletion removed the measured barium-sensitive inward-rectifier current in isolated capillary endothelial cells relative to wild type. The record identifies Kir2.1, not a general glial potassium-uptake process.

Cortical 15 mM potassium increased relative perfusion, with a smaller response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium further reduced responses; this cortical exposure is distinct from focal capillary injection.

Whisker stimulation evoked a smaller relative cortical perfusion response after endothelial-targeted Kcnj2 deletion, with residual responses present. Barium reduced responses further and is not restricted to capillary endothelium.

Posttetanic potentiation over 0-2 min and short-term potentiation over 0-15 min were greater in Kir4.1 cKO slices than controls. The study does not uniquely assign this effect to potassium handling rather than glutamate handling or developmental changes.

Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller TBOA-sensitive inward-current magnitudes in the presence of Ba2+ than controls. The developmental intervention and subtraction assay do not isolate a unique molecular mechanism of clearance.

Kir4.1 cKO passive astrocytes had smaller Ba2+-sensitive inward-current magnitudes during the stated Schaffer stimulation protocol than controls. This is an electrical uptake proxy, not a direct extracellular potassium measurement.
Brief bilateral LC photostimulation promotes EEG/EMG-defined sleep-to-wake transitions in the inactive-period assay.
Hour-long LC photoinhibition reduces active-period wakefulness and wake-episode duration while leaving sleep-to-wake transitions possible.

The place-trained group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups. Counts of all degenerating profiles do not establish survival of individually tracked newborn neurons, and the exact terminal cohort for this paragraph is unresolved.

At 24 hours after training, the place group had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than naive, cue and time-yoked swimming groups, with six animals per group. This is an effect of the specified training comparison on previously labeled cells; a unique survival mechanism was not isolated.

The trace-paired group had fewer morphologically pyknotic subgranular profiles than naive and unpaired groups. These are total degenerating profiles, not an identified newborn-neuron survival fraction. The printed ANOVA degrees of freedom and terminal-cohort allocation remain unresolved.

At 24 hours after four training days, trace-paired rats had more dentate BrdU-labeled cells than unpaired and naive controls, with six animals per group. BrdU preceded training by one week. The measured endpoint is retained labeled cells, not a separately identified increase in division rate.
Motion-task choices show an early contraversive bias after LIP suppression, with reported attenuation over trials and sessions.
LIP microstimulation shifts choices toward the selected response field and changes response times directionally.
LIP silencing shifts free choices away from contralateral targets and increases contralateral saccade endpoint error in the control task.

The main 0.5 mg/kg LPS challenge increased bulk Vglut2-cre cNST calcium-response area relative to the preceding saline session. Fixed session order and a population fluorescence measurement limit causal and cellular interpretation.

Peripheral LPS produced more cNST FOS-positive neurons than saline at two hours in the specified counting region. The marker response does not establish DBH-specific firing or identify the peripheral mediator.
MCT2 antisense reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. This regional knockdown is not a cell-restricted neuronal intervention.

L-lactate rescued the reported MCT4-ODN-associated retention deficit at the tested 24 h and 7 day endpoints. Rescue supports a lactate-related contribution without uniquely establishing an exclusive fuel pathway.

MCT4 antisense treatment reduced inhibitory-avoidance retention latency at 24 h and 7 days relative to scrambled controls. Acquisition latency was not significantly changed. The behavioral result does not directly measure astrocyte-to-neuron lactate flux.

Deprived optic nerves had lower CAP-derived conduction velocity and broader length-normalized CAP responses than paired controls. The experiment changes visual experience, not only myelin internode length.

Myelin internodes generated during deprivation were reported shorter than open-eye controls. Text and caption disagree on the deprived median, so no exact median or quantitative geometry rule is assigned.

The deprived optic nerve and tract had more CC1-positive mature oligodendrocytes than the respective controls. This endpoint does not establish increased total myelin thickness or a universally stabilizing glial property.

In the subsequent primitive-pair task, every tested geometric rule has shorter reported recognition time and fewer missed violations than the unrelated-pair control. Rotations by three steps are harder on selected measures than some other primitives, contradicting equal behavioral cost as a general assumption for this task.

In the selected adult sample, recognition repetitions, violation-response time and missed violations increase with assigned sequence complexity, including analyses excluding the irregular template. Published AIC selection also retains the presence of rotation by three steps for recognition and response time, and spatial distance for misses; description cost alone is not a complete behavioral account.

CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation increased microglial fluorescence near labeled cortical boutons relative to control conditions. This is a morphological proximity readout, not direct synaptic inhibition.

In the neonatal microglial culture assay, ARL67156 treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.

In the neonatal microglial culture assay, APCP treatment reduced measured medium adenosine after ATP exposure relative to the vehicle condition. This is a pharmacological culture contrast, not a cell-exclusive adult mechanism.
CNO exposure in the hM3Dq thalamocortical preparation reduced microglial process-tip velocity while bouton proximity increased. Lower tip velocity and directed recruitment are different measurements.

After a targeted capillary lesion, nearby microglial processes switched toward the injured site and accumulated around it. This measures a local morphological response, not demonstrated neuronal protection.

Adults pretrained in adolescent reaching showed increased formation and elimination during a new capellini task compared with general adult controls: 8.7 versus 3.7 percent formation and 9.0 versus 4.0 percent elimination, five versus six mice. This is a compound task-history comparison.

Of spines first seen between days zero and four, 42.3 percent persisted to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up in mice trained for sixteen days, versus 13.5 percent in controls, five mice per group. Survival of this selected new-spine subset supports finite structural persistence, not permanence or memory necessity.

Naive adults learning capellini handling had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.8 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 8.2 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. This task is separate from single-seed reaching.

Naive adults learning the reaching task had greater four-day formation and elimination than controls: reported formation 7.9 versus 3.7 percent and elimination 9.5 versus 4.0 percent, five trained versus six control mice. The result does not supply an age-independent remodeling rate.

Over four days, reaching-trained adolescent mice had greater spine formation and elimination than controls. Table S1 reports formation 13.3 versus 6.0 percent and elimination 13.7 versus 9.0 percent, with 25 trained and 18 control mice. These are interval-specific morphological responses in sampled dendrites.
Retinotopically matched MT silencing impairs motion direction sensitivity; moving the stimulus outside the affected field restores performance in the reported control.
Optogenetic NE-MO activation increased L-MO radial astrocyte calcium fluorescence in the selected larval fish preparation.
NE-MO activation reduced fictive swimming in fish with intact radial astrocytes, following a possible brief increase in swim vigor. The glia-ablated condition is a separate null result.
The neuroligin-contact intervention induces the local presynaptic-differentiation readout in the cited preparation.

Perforant-path stimulation evoked postsynaptic responses in four sampled birth-labeled neurons. Spontaneous input was also observed in six cells. These afferent responses do not establish functional axonal output to the downstream circuit.

Running-housed mice had more BrdU-labeled dentate cells than standard-housed mice in the separate 48-hour assay. BrdU incorporation does not itself count mature neurons or show that learning is necessary for neurogenesis.
DL-APV affects CA1 potentiation induction in the cited preparation, with basal transmission treated separately.

assertion: Figure 4f source counts report seizures in 9/11 P2ry12 knockout mice versus 3/13 controls after D1 agonist. The genotype contrast is not a cell-selective perturbation of microglial sensing.

Extraintestinal cytokine perfusion evoked repeatable calcium responses in sampled nodose neurons. Repeated responses in this preparation support stimulus sensitivity but do not establish direct receptor binding or a complete immune feedback loop.
Whisker-evoked responses depend on sensory-input phase relative to the experimentally induced gamma cycle.

Striatal dialysate adenosine was lower in the PLX5622 group than in controls in the anesthetized microdialysis assay. The source workbook supplies five independent mouse rows per group in ng/mL and a separate nM conversion.

PLX5622-treated mice showed increased distance-dependent correlations and thresholded synchrony of striatal calcium events at baseline relative to controls. Correlated activity is the measured outcome; it does not identify direct neuronal connections.
Practice in the imposed force field brings reaching paths toward their baseline shape in the reported task.

Within the isolated housing condition, PV activation lowers EdU-positive density, MCM2-positive density and the MCM2-positive RGL fraction compared with isolated no-light controls. This treatment contrast is distinct from comparing the two housing groups under light.

Under PV light stimulation, isolated mice retain higher EdU-positive RGL density than group-housed mice in Figure 5c, with reported P < 0.05. This residual housing contrast prevents a claim that PV activation abolishes every measured isolation effect.

Five-day PV inhibition increases EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. Increased marker counts do not establish successful maturation, integration or a universal neural-activity requirement.

Five-day PV activation lowers EdU-positive RGL density, MCM2-positive RGL density and the MCM2-positive fraction relative to no-light sham. The endpoint is suppression of the measured cycle markers, not reduced mature-neuron production measured across the full lineage.

PV photostimulation evokes a tonic RGL current that is blocked by bicuculline and enhanced by vigabatrin in the tested slices. This is a GABA-sensitive clamp-current response, not RGL spiking, cell-cycle entry or a measured one-to-one synapse.

The five-day systemic diazepam comparison lowers EdU-positive and MCM2-positive RGL densities and the MCM2-positive fraction. Systemic treatment does not by itself identify a selective RGL receptor mechanism or measure completed neuron production.

Conditional gamma2 deletion increases assigned activated clones at two and seven days. At seven days, R+R and R+astrocyte classes increase while the R+intermediate-progenitor comparison is nonsignificant. The class distribution is not a uniform increase in neuronal production.

At thirty days, conditional gamma2 deletion changes the assigned clone composition, including more R+R and no-R clones and fewer single-R and neuronal or multilineage classes. Later lineage effects and unresolved denominators prevent conversion to founder transition probabilities.
In the selected WT-background TWISP preparation, SAADL activation produced decreased downstream OLLR calcium activity (Randi et al. 2023, Figure 1).

In 23 French adults, every selected regular category has lower mean error than the irregular baseline, including the first presentation's positions 6-8. The effect concerns these stimulus contrasts under corrective feedback, not recovery of a complete unseen program from one exposure.

In the 24-child Experiment 2 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs, two-squares and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. This is task-specific success with selected patterns; it does not establish possession of every proposed primitive.

In the separate 44-adult behavioral experiment, average anticipation index increases with assigned sequence description cost (reported R squared 0.86, P<0.001): simpler templates have less normalized gaze error at target onset. Repeat and alternate patterns show an advantage over irregular from the fourth and seventh locations of the first presentation respectively.

In the 20-participant Munduruku cohort, all tested regular categories except two-crosses have lower overall error than the irregular baseline. The two-arcs boundary at position 13 is below baseline; two-squares and diagonal-position contrasts remain uneven. The cohort combines adolescents and adults.

In the separate 23-child Experiment 3 cohort, repeat, repeat+2, two-arcs and four-segments sequences have lower mean error than the irregular baseline. Two complete previews precede each block, followed by the same corrective task.

At one week, sampled dendrites had lower spine density than controls: reported 1.81 versus 2.23 spines per ten micrometers, four versus six mice. This spatial density is distinct from the increased percentage of new protrusions during the acute six-hour assay.

At one week after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 1.37, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

At 2 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.93, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

At 6 weeks after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 0.75, versus 0.14 in controls; 3 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

Six weeks after photothrombosis, fluorescent vascular volume fraction was higher than in controls: reported 7.25 versus 4.36 percent, t(8)=3.14, P<0.01. This volume-occupancy result does not count new vessels or establish a selectively tested angiogenesis mechanism.

The group-II metabotropic glutamate receptor agonist DCG-IV suppressed light-evoked postsynaptic responses in two experiments, consistent with mossy-fiber involvement. This does not locate every synaptic hop or establish a universal connection strength.

Kynurenic acid blocked light-evoked postsynaptic responses in eight tested targets. Dependence on glutamatergic transmission can occur upstream of an inhibitory relay, so blockade does not make every recorded response a direct excitatory synapse.

Light pulses evoke spikes in selected ChR2-labeled dentate neurons. Opsin expression and age affect capture and latency; this is an imposed activation protocol, not endogenous firing or a universal maturation threshold.
